text:
**30W is the minimum for a MacBook Air, and 70W or more is what you need for fast charging.**

- **Minimum to charge:** Apple's M5 MacBook Air spec lists 30W as the minimum wattage required to charge ([Apple specs](https://images.apple.com/tm/macbook-air/specs/)).
- **What ships in the box:**
  - M4 with 8-core GPU: 30W adapter.
  - M4 with 10-core GPU: 35W dual-port adapter ([Apple M4 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/122209)).
  - 13-inch M5: 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max ([Apple M5 specs](https://fd.xuwubk.eu.org/https/support.apple.com/en-us/126320)).
- **Fast charging:** The M4 and M5 Airs are fast-charge capable with a 70W or higher USB PD power source. Apple also sells a 70W adapter as an option.
- **Third-party chargers:** Any USB-C charger that supports USB Power Delivery works, even at higher or lower wattage than Apple's recommendation. For the best experience, Apple suggests at least the wattage of the adapter recommended for your model ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109509)).

To check which Air you have and what it needs, look at the 2022-or-later list on Apple's page. The 15-inch models list 35W, 67W, and 70W options, and the 30W adapter is 13-inch only.

**A third-party option:** The [Baseus GaN5 Pro 65W charger](https://dealectric.com/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u) (2-pack, $49.99 at Baseus's US store per the listing, verified 2026-10-21) has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A port. [Buy it here](https://dealectric.com/go/baseus-gan5-pro-65w-2c-u). That's an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Two caveats:

- At 65W it's above the 30W minimum but below the 70W Apple lists for fast charging, so you may not get full fast-charge speed.
- With two or three devices plugged in, the laptop port drops to 45W, which is still enough to charge an Air.

If you want fast charging, look for a 70W-or-higher USB PD charger. If you just want a reliable everyday or travel charger, 30W to 65W is fine.
